headline: `env -i PATH="$PATH"` TOOK AWAY NOTHING THAT FAILS OPEN, AND I ATTACKED IT BY CONSTRUCTION RATHER THAN BY READING. LOCALE IS THE HEADLINE RESULT AND IT IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE FEAR: the stage is now MORE deterministic, not less. Over a purpose-built repository carrying real UTF-8 filenames, UTF-8 content, a latin-1 coding cookie, a cp1251 cookie, an undecodable high byte, a multibyte shell file and a non-ASCII shell filename, the boundary text and the round-4 text produce BYTE-IDENTICAL stdout and BYTE-IDENTICAL stderr, and they stay byte-identical under six ambient settings (LC_ALL=C, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8, LC_ALL=C with LANG=C, PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii, PYTHONUTF8=0 with LC_ALL=C). THE MECHANISM, MEASURED: at the boundary CPython's PEP 538 coercion plus PEP 540 give sys.flags.utf8_mode=1 and utf-8 for filesystem, default and stdio encodings UNCONDITIONALLY, and they still do with coercion forced off, which is the adopter machine that has no C.UTF-8 locale. Source encoding never depended on locale in the first place: the stage reads bytes with open(path, "rb") and hands them to source_to_code, so PEP 263 cookies are honoured by the compiler. `bash -n` returns the same verdict on multibyte, invalid-UTF-8 and $'...' shell files under C, C.UTF-8 and en_US.UTF-8. THE THREE GIT HOLES REPRODUCE EXACTLY AND ARE CLOSED: GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE and GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS each give `lint: pass (0 python, 0 shell, 0.00s)` exit 0 on the round-4 text over a six-defect tree and each names every defect with exit 1 on the shipped text. A FOURTH IS ALSO CLOSED AND IT IS THE ONE ROUND 4 CALLED UNCLOSABLE: PYTHONPATH carrying a hostile subprocess.py is a false pass on the round-4 text and fails closed on the shipped text, and so is PYTHONPATH carrying a hostile sitecustomize.py. PYTHONHOME does fail closed at both revisions, so round 5's third correction is right. WHAT I FOUND, AND IT IS A NOTE AND NOT A BLOCK: stripping HOME makes GLOBAL git config unreachable, which costs a working workaround for a PRE-EXISTING non-ASCII-path bug, and makes safe.directory reachable only from /etc/gitconfig. It fails CLOSED, loudly, in a direction that cannot hand out a pass, over a surface this repository does not have. Two record sentences overstate. NOTHING BLOCKS. GATE GREEN AT 3201 / 0 ON MY OWN RUN.

THE ROUND EXISTS TO REPLACE A FALSE SENTENCE WITH A MEASUREMENT AND IT DOES, AND THE CLOSURE IS WIDER THAN THE THREE NAMES IT ADVERTISES. I built a throwaway repository with six planted defects plus the shipped stage and a round-4 copy differing from it by exactly the boundary token, and attacked both. FALSE PASS ON THE ROUND-4 TEXT, exit 0 with an EMPTY failing set and `lint: pass (0 python, 0 shell, 0.00s)`: GIT_DIR at an empty repository, GIT_INDEX_FILE at that repository's index, GIT_INDEX_FILE at a path that does not exist at all (a broader instance than the manifest's construction), GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS=1, PYTHONPATH at a directory holding a hostile subprocess.py, and PYTHONPATH at a directory holding a hostile sitecustomize.py. CLOSED ON THE SHIPPED TEXT: every one of those gives exit 1 and names all six defects, identical to a clean run. ALSO MEASURED CLOSED at both revisions, so they were never false-pass routes and the boundary is not what saves them: GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY and GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS individually AND as the three-variable combination, PYTHONHOME, WARP_LINT_LIST, WARP_LINT_SKIP, CDPATH, PYTHONSTARTUP, PYTHONWARNINGS, PYTHONINSPECT, PYTHONDONTWRITEBYTECODE, GIT_CEILING_DIRECTORIES, ENV and IFS. STILL A FALSE PASS AT BOTH REVISIONS AND CORRECTLY DECLARED: BASH_ENV, which exits 0 printing an attacker-chosen summary line. `--list` exits 2 with 12 file lines on stdout and ZERO `lint:` lines on stdout; `--bogus` exits 2 with the usage line. THE ANTI-DRIFT PIN ON THE PYCACHE COPY IS REAL, PROVEN BY DRIFTING IT: I changed the shipped `CDPATH= cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."` line to `CDPATH= cd "$(dirname "$0")/../"`, which is the shape a maintainer would produce, and the full suite went to 3197 passed / 4 failed including the bytecode probe, because the assertion requires each substitution target to occur EXACTLY ONCE and requires reversing both substitutions to reproduce the shipped text byte for byte. The copy cannot silently diverge.

THE BOUNDARY COSTS NOTHING AND I MEASURED THE INCREMENT PROPERLY, WHICH TOOK TWO ATTEMPTS. My first attempt timed a copy of the stage placed OUTSIDE the repository, so its `cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."` landed on a non-repository, git failed and the run finished in 0.05s: a measurement of nothing, discarded and reported rather than published. Redone with both texts inside the SAME pristine detached worktree at 0814a28, `/usr/bin/time -f %e bash scripts/<stage>`: WITH the boundary 0.83 / 0.83 / 0.82, WITHOUT it 0.83 / 0.82 / 0.83, and both print the SAME corpus, `lint: pass (694 python, 172 shell, 0.80s)` and `(694 python, 172 shell, 0.81s)`. So `env -i` is inside the noise, single runs and not best-of. AC3's bar is under 2 seconds. THE CORRECTED RATIO IS ARITHMETICALLY RIGHT WITH BOTH ENDS FROM THE SAME COMMAND: 13.89 / 0.85 = 16.34x and 14.55 / 0.81 = 17.96x, which is the published 16.3x to 18.0x, and the retired 18.4x ceiling requires an after-figure of 0.791, which is an internally printed value and not an externally measured one, exactly as the round describes its own error. THE GATE ON MY OWN CLOCK, `/usr/bin/time -v ./scripts/verify.sh` in a detached worktree at 0814a28 with the timing output written OUTSIDE that worktree: GATE GREEN, exit 0, 3:09.89 wall clock, 37 percent CPU on 20 cores, 305212 KB peak RSS, selftest 3201 passed / 0 failed, catalog 5 run / 18 not-applicable / 0 waived / 0 undeclared. That is 0.19s from the builder's 3:09.70 at 0738961 and inside the ten-run 3:08.56 to 3:10.22 spread the manifest publishes.

notes: N1 THE ONE THING `env -i` GENUINELY TOOK AWAY, AND MY MOST IMPORTANT FINDING. Stripping HOME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME and GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL makes GLOBAL git config unreachable to `git ls-files`, and I proved the mechanism rather than inferring it: with HOME pointing at a fixture holding `[core] quotePath = false`, `git config --get core.quotePath` returns `false` ambiently and returns NOTHING with exit 1 under `env -i PATH="$PATH" HOME=<fixture>` removed, and the same holds for `safe.directory` and for the XDG_CONFIG_HOME route. THE OBSERVABLE COST, measured on the shipped text at scripts/check_lint.sh:79 over a repository with three real UTF-8 tracked filenames and a global `core.quotePath=false`: the round-4 text lints `cafe_ok.py` correctly and names the genuinely broken `cafe_bad.py` with its real SyntaxError, while the shipped text falls back to quotePath=true, receives `"caf\303\251_ok.py"` from git, and emits THREE spurious `   FAIL:` lines plus a FileNotFoundError where the real diagnostic should be. THE SECOND HALF IS THE CI ONE: `safe.directory` is deliberately NOT honoured from a repository's own config, so under this boundary it can only be set in /etc/gitconfig, and a uid-mismatched container checkout, the ordinary GitHub Actions and GitLab runner shape whose documented remedy is `git config --global --add safe.directory`, now has no per-user remedy. I could not force the uid mismatch to measure it end to end because user namespaces are blocked in my sandbox (`unshare --map-root-user` fails writing /proc/self/uid_map), so I measured the config-reachability mechanism instead and state the consequence as a deduction from it, labelled as one. WHY THIS IS A NOTE AND NOT A BLOCK, on four legs. (1) DIRECTION: it fails CLOSED and loudly. Every observed outcome is exit 1 with named paths or exit non-zero with a traceback; no construction I found turns a HOME-dependent setting into a pass, which is the property this item exists to hold. (2) PRE-EXISTING: the underlying non-ASCII-path bug is in all three revisions. `git show 7df08a1:scripts/check_lint.sh` iterates `$(git ls-files '*.py')`, so the per-file loop this replaced is broken on quoted paths AND on word-split paths identically, and both the round-4 and shipped texts fail those files under DEFAULT config. Round 5 removed a workaround for someone else's bug, it did not write the bug. (3) EMPTY SURFACE HERE: `git ls-files | grep -cP '"'` is 0 in this repository, no tracked path is quoted, no global core.quotePath is set, and `git ls-files '*.py'` and `'*.sh'` return byte-identical lists with and without HOME at 694 and 172. A fresh clone with stock config behaves identically to round 4. (4) A REMEDY SURVIVES: LOCAL .git/config IS still read under the boundary, which I measured by setting core.quotePath=false locally and watching the shipped text and the round-4 text produce identical correct output. WHAT I WOULD DO ABOUT IT, for the owner and not as a condition of landing: name HOME in the header beside BASH_ENV and PATH as a thing the boundary deliberately removes and what it costs, or pass `GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM` through by name if the CI shape ever bites. Both are one-line changes and neither is worth a sixth round.

N2 THE ENVIRONMENT AT THE BOUNDARY HOLDS TWO VARIABLES, NOT ONE, AND THE MANIFEST SAYS ONE. Measured: `env -i PATH=/usr/bin:/bin python3 -c 'import os; print(dict(os.environ))'` prints `{'PATH': '/usr/bin:/bin', 'LC_CTYPE': 'C.UTF-8'}`, and `subprocess.run(['env'])` from inside the boundary shows the CHILDREN inherit both, so `git ls-files` and `bash -n` start from PATH and LC_CTYPE. CPython's PEP 538 coercion sets that second variable during startup. checks[2] of the round-5 manifest reads `the environment its interpreter and children start from holds exactly ONE variable, PATH', which is therefore false as written for the children and loose for the interpreter. THE SECURITY PROPERTY IS INTACT AND I PROVED IT SEPARATELY, which is why this is wording and not a defect: the added variable is a CONSTANT the interpreter manufactures and is provably not attacker-controlled, because ambient LC_CTYPE values of `hostile.VALUE`, `tr_TR.UTF-8`, `C` and `en_US.ISO-8859-1` ALL yield exactly `LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8` and fsencoding utf-8 inside. Note also that the SHIPPED TEXT is the precise one: scripts/check_lint.sh:60 to :61 says `ONE variable crosses the boundary, by name', which is exactly true. Only the manifest overstates, and the fix is to say `exactly one variable CROSSES the boundary, and CPython adds a constant LC_CTYPE=C.UTF-8 of its own'.

N3 A COUNTERFACTUAL IN THE RECORD NAMES FOUR VARIABLES THAT WERE NEVER OPEN. criteria AC2 evidence[1] argues the `env=` alternative `would have closed GIT_DIR and GIT_INDEX_FILE and left GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS, GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY, GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS and PYTHONPATH open'. MEASURED ON THE ROUND-4 TEXT over the six-defect tree: GIT_WORK_TREE, GIT_COMMON_DIR, GIT_OBJECT_DIRECTORY and GIT_ICASE_PATHSPECS each exit 1 naming all six defects, and so does the three-variable combination the manifest itself cites elsewhere. None of the four is a false-pass route, individually or together, so `open' in the false-pass sense that the same sentence uses for GIT_DIR is wrong for four of its six names. GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS and PYTHONPATH are correct and I reproduced both. THE EXACT SET, since the item's own discipline is that the sentence comes from the output: the false-pass routes on the round-4 text are GIT_DIR, GIT_INDEX_FILE, GIT_LITERAL_PATHSPECS, PYTHONPATH, BASH_ENV and PATH. Round 5 closes the first four and declares the last two. This is the class the last four reviews have each caught once and the resolution is to DELETE the four names from that clause, not to add a residual. It changes nothing about the fix, which closes the class regardless of which members of it happened to be exploitable.

N4 `set -u` DOES NOT PROTECT THE ONE VARIABLE THE STAGE NOW DEPENDS ON, and the failure mode is closed by something else. The natural reading of `set -u` at scripts/check_lint.sh:77 followed by `"$PATH"` at :79 is that an unset PATH is caught. It is not: bash ALWAYS defines PATH, supplying its compiled default when the environment has none. Measured, `env -u PATH bash -c 'set -u; echo $PATH'` prints /usr/local/sbin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/sbin:/usr/bin:/sbin:/bin, and `env -u PATH bash scripts/check_lint.sh` runs the stage CORRECTLY to a full verdict rather than failing. That is a fine outcome, it is simply not the mechanism the text implies. EVERY OTHER PATH DEGRADATION FAILS CLOSED and I walked all of them with an absolute /bin/bash so the harness could not be what failed: PATH empty gives exit 127 with `/env: No such file or directory' and no stdout; PATH holding env, git, bash and dirname but no python3 gives exit 127 with `env: python3: No such file or directory'; PATH without git gives exit 1 on FileNotFoundError with empty stdout; PATH without bash gives exit 1 after naming the python failures. Not one produces a `lint: pass'.

N5 THE ADOPTER ORDERING WORKS AND I CHECKED THE THING THAT LOOKS LIKE A BOOTSTRAP PROBLEM. `env` must be found BEFORE the new PATH exists, and it is: bash resolves `env` against the OUTER PATH. Measured by planting a distinct copy at $TMP/envdir/env and running `env PATH=$TMP/envdir:/usr/bin:/bin bash -c 'command -v env; exec env -i PATH="$PATH" sh -c "echo inner PATH=\$PATH; command -v python3"'`, which resolves the planted /envdir/env, passes the full outer PATH inward, and finds /usr/bin/python3 inside. Both `env -i` and `env NAME=VALUE command` are POSIX, `env` is a real executable and not a shell builtin on this system (/usr/bin/env and /bin/env, GNU coreutils 9.4), and the boundary line assumes no git version and no GNU extension. The one genuine machine assumption is a `python3` on PATH, which the stage had before this round.

N6 THE TWO REPORTED INTERACTIONS ARE GENUINELY FIXED, THEY FAILED LOUDLY RATHER THAN SILENTLY, AND NEITHER LEFT A RESIDUE. I re-broke each in an isolated worktree and ran the FULL suite. (a) HEREDOC HALVES: restoring the old `startswith("exec python3")` opener match at scripts/selftest.py:20750 against the new opener gives 3200 passed / 1 failed, and the ONE failure is the both-halves environment guard. So the interaction was a loud red and not a silent degradation, which is the important part, because a silent one would have disarmed every python-half tooth. The fix is also non-vacuous at HEAD: the shape match `startswith("exec ") and endswith("<<'PY'")` finds the opener at index 78 and the closer at 189, splitting the file into an 80-line shell half and a 110-line python half that contains `def check_python`, where the OLD predicate finds ZERO openers and would classify the whole file as shell. (b) BYTECODE PROBE: covered under AC2 and under N7's matrix; it is pinned by a reversal assertion with teeth.

N7 THE BOUNDARY LINE CANNOT BE REMOVED SILENTLY, AND I DELETED IT TWO WAYS TO PROVE IT. In separate detached worktrees at 0814a28, full suite each time. REVERTING the boundary to `exec python3`, which is the shape a maintainer or a bad revert would produce: 3197 passed / 4 failed, tripping the both-halves environment guard (via the shell pin, whose third pinned line IS the boundary), the four-tooth guard assertion, the new git-environment differential, and the real-corpus bytecode probe. DELETING the whole line: 3183 passed / 18 failed. So the line is pinned by at least three independent assertions, and the `_L07_SRC.count('exec env -i PATH="$PATH" python3') == 1` conjunct means it cannot be duplicated either. Together with the drift mutation under AC2 that makes four mutations, each caught, each loudly.

N8 THE THREE RECORD CORRECTIONS ARE ALL CORRECT AND I DERIVED EVERY COUNT MYSELF. THE SPAN: round 4 does contain the literal `13.96 TO 14.55' and the literal `18.4', and the corrected span 13.89 to 14.55 over five enumerated measurers is arithmetically consistent with the ratio 16.3x to 18.0x as shown under AC3. THE NOTE COUNT: `len(json.load(...)['notes'])` gives verdict-fail 7 notes with 2 must-fix, verdict-2 10 with 0, verdict-3 EIGHT with 0, verdict-4 10 with 0. So round 4's `TWO OF ITS TEN NOTES' of verdict-3 was indeed wrong and eight is right, and ten is verdict-2's. THE OVER-DECLARATION: PYTHONHOME=/nonexistent gives exit 1 with NO summary line on the round-4 text, so it fails closed and never belonged in a false-pass list, which the round-4 reviewer had itself measured. ASSERTION_INTEGRITY NOW MATCHES MEASUREMENT: it retires round 4's `Three classes do' and states four at round 4, which my matrix confirms exactly as BASH_ENV, PATH, PYTHONPATH and the git-variable class, leaving BASH_ENV and PATH after this round, both of which I re-measured. Subject only to N2 and N3, the two sentences that still overstate.

N9 CARRIED FORWARD, NOT INTRODUCED BY THIS ROUND, RECORDED BECAUSE N1 SLIGHTLY WIDENS ITS REACH. When `git ls-files` itself fails, the stage dies on the `check=True` at scripts/check_lint.sh:103 with a raw CalledProcessError traceback, EMPTY stdout and NO `lint:` line at all. Measured by running the stage from a directory that is not a repository: exit 1, stdout empty, `returned non-zero exit status 128`. The gate reads the exit status so this is RED and correct, but it is the shape a dubious-ownership CI checkout would now present, and the operator reading the log sees a python traceback rather than a lint verdict. This has been true since round 1 and is out of scope. Round-1 N4 also still stands unfixed and declared: neither stage handles a tracked path containing a space, and I note the same class covers non-ASCII paths, with no such path tracked in either case.

N10 THE FLOOR IS CLEAN ON EVERY ITEM AND ALL OF IT IS MINE. Gate GREEN at 0814a28, exit 0, 3:09.89, 3201 passed / 0 failed, catalog 5 / 18 / 0 / 0. `wc -l .warp/metrics.py` is 399 and metrics.py appears in NO numstat of `cf20743~1..0814a28`. scripts/verify.sh and plugin/templates/scripts/verify.sh are both BYTE-IDENTICAL to 7df08a1 by `git show <rev>:<path> | cmp -`. The footprint derived rather than remembered: `git log --format='' --name-only cf20743~1..0738961 | sort -u` is exactly TEN paths over `git rev-list --count` NINE commits, and the same range to 0814a28 is ELEVEN paths over TEN commits, the eleventh being verdict-4-pass_with_notes.json. None of the seven protected_paths in .warp/policy.yaml is among them and none of the four frozen safety-core modules (authorization.py, two_key.py, policy_check.py, decision.py) is either. RULE #1 over the fix commit's 90 added lines: 0 em dashes, 0 en dashes, 0 non-ASCII bytes, 0 lines carrying a double hyphen. proof_digest recomputes to sha256:1afc1d90cc9e5579 and matches the recorded value. `validate.py all`, `validate.py proof proof/WARP-0711/manifest.json` and `validate.py verdict` on all four committed verdicts each exit 0 silently. supersedes_verdict chains correctly across all five manifests (round 1 none, then verdict-fail, verdict-2, verdict-3, verdict-4) and supersedes chains correctly across all four verdicts, with each manifest's commit field matching its own fix commit. Every line-numbered citation in the ROUND-5 manifest resolves at the revision it names: check_lint.sh:80 at cfae9b2 and :92 at 0814a28 are both the SIGPIPE restoration, py_compile.py:146 is `except Exception as err:`, baseline.md:4 is the /tmp/gateprof provenance line. HEAD is 0814a28, origin/main is still 7df08a1 and 10 behind, nothing was pushed, the working tree is clean, the spec is at status ready, and no verdict was written by the builder. HOUSEKEEPING: the builder's scratchpad/r5-fix worktree was already gone when I arrived; I created six worktrees, removed all six with `git worktree remove --force` plus `git worktree prune`, and `git worktree list` ends at exactly THREE, the main tree plus warp-worktrees/WARP-0623 and /tmp/warp-w7-rev, neither of them this item's. I wrote NO file into the worktree I gated: the `/usr/bin/time -v` output went to a scratchpad path outside it, and the only modifications the gated tree ended with are .warp/events.jsonl and .warp/last_verify, both written by the gate itself.

residual_rulings.DID `env -i` BREAK LOCALE: NO, AND IT IS THE STRONGEST RESULT IN THIS PASS: the stage is MORE deterministic with the environment stripped, not less. Byte-for-byte stdout AND stderr equality between the shipped text and a round-4 copy over a repository holding three real UTF-8 filenames (created with $'...' after I caught my own first probe writing literal backslash-x sequences and discarded it), a UTF-8 comment and string, a latin-1 coding cookie, a cp1251 coding cookie, a high byte with NO cookie, a multibyte shell file and a non-ASCII shell filename. Equality holds again under LC_ALL=C, LC_ALL=C.UTF-8, LC_ALL=en_US.UTF-8, LC_ALL=C with LANG=C, PYTHONIOENCODING=ascii, and PYTHONUTF8=0 with LC_ALL=C. THE REASON IS STRUCTURAL AND MEASURED IN THREE PLACES. (1) The interpreter: at the boundary sys.flags.utf8_mode is 1 where ambiently it is 0, and filesystem, default and stdio encodings are utf-8 with surrogateescape; with PYTHONCOERCECLOCALE=0 forced, which is the adopter machine lacking a C.UTF-8 locale, utf8_mode is STILL 1 and every encoding is STILL utf-8, so PEP 540 covers the case PEP 538 cannot. (2) Source decoding never depended on locale: check_python opens with "rb" at scripts/check_lint.sh:133 and passes bytes to source_to_code at :135, so PEP 263 cookies are the compiler's business and both cookie fixtures compile clean at every setting. (3) The shell half: `bash -n` returns exit 0 identically on multibyte, invalid-UTF-8 and $'\u...' files under C, C.UTF-8 and en_US.UTF-8, and byte-identical stderr through the boundary. The repository's earlier locale-dependent result is not reachable here.
residual_rulings.DID `env -i` BREAK HOME OR GIT CONFIG: PARTLY, AND IT IS N1, MY TOP FINDING, AND IT IS A NOTE. Global git config is unreachable: with a fixture HOME holding core.quotePath=false, precomposeUnicode, excludesFile and user identity, the shipped text ignores all of it while the round-4 text honours it, and the observable delta over a repository with non-ASCII tracked paths is THREE spurious `   FAIL:` lines plus a FileNotFoundError displacing a real SyntaxError. GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL is likewise ignored, XDG_CONFIG_HOME likewise. safe.directory becomes settable only in /etc/gitconfig because git refuses it from a repository's own config, which is the CI shape I could not force to measure (user namespaces blocked) and state as a deduction from the config-reachability measurement. AGAINST THAT: git emits NO warning and NO stdout pollution with HOME absent (stderr is 0 bytes, exit 0), the file list is BYTE-IDENTICAL with and without HOME at 694 python and 172 shell, LOCAL .git/config is still honoured so a per-repository remedy survives, the underlying non-ASCII bug is present in the per-file loop at 7df08a1 and under default config in every revision, this repository tracks ZERO quoted paths, and every failure is CLOSED. No construction I attempted turned a HOME-dependent setting into a pass. Not blocking; worth one header sentence.
residual_rulings.IS THE PYCACHE-PREFIX COPY SOUND, AND CA: SOUND, AND IT CANNOT DRIFT WITHOUT GOING RED, WHICH I PROVED BY MAKING IT DRIFT. The probe writes a copy of the shipped text with exactly two substitutions, the prefix injected into the boundary line and an absolute `cd` because the copy lives outside the repository, and the assertion requires each ORIGINAL substring to occur exactly once in the shipped text, requires the copy to differ from it, requires the substitution list to have length 2, and requires reversing BOTH substitutions to reproduce the shipped text EXACTLY. Both replacement strings embed a fresh temporary path or the absolute ROOT, so neither can collide with unrelated text and the reversal is well defined. TEETH MEASURED: changing the shipped cd line to `"$(dirname "$0")/../"` breaks the occurs-exactly-once conjunct and the suite goes to 3197 / 4 with the bytecode probe among the failures. NON-VACUITY SURVIVES THE BOUNDARY: 28 stdlib cache entries land in the private prefix while zero mirror this repository, so the probe is still proven able to observe a write, which is precisely why stripping the variable made it FAIL rather than pass empty. The python half and the corpus under test are the shipped ones; only where a hypothetical .pyc would land differs.
residual_rulings.IS THE PATH DEPENDENCE CLOSED: YES IN EVERY DIRECTION THAT MATTERS, AND N4 CORRECTS THE MECHANISM. PATH unset is not a failure at all because bash supplies its compiled default and the stage runs correctly, so `set -u` is not what guards line 79. PATH empty gives 127, PATH without python3 gives 127, without git gives 1, without bash gives 1, and none of the four prints a `lint: pass`. A hostile python3 earlier on PATH IS a false pass, which round 2 conceded, which the shipped text concedes in writing at :61 to :63, and which is identically true of the round-4 text and of the per-file loop this replaced. The boundary's dependence on exactly one inherited variable does not create a new failure mode; it makes the pre-existing one the only one.

disposition: LAND IT. NO BLOCKING DEFECT, AND NO SIXTH ROUND FOR WHAT I FOUND. The one genuinely open question was what the blunt boundary took away, and I attacked it by construction on every surface the brief named. LOCALE, the sharpest one, is not merely unbroken: the boundary forces UTF-8 mode on unconditionally, including on a machine with no C.UTF-8 locale, and the stage's source decoding never depended on locale because it reads bytes and lets the compiler honour PEP 263. `bash -n` is indifferent. PATH degrades closed in four shapes and its one open shape is the conceded one, documented on the line itself. The `env` bootstrap ordering works and the boundary is POSIX with no new machine assumption. The pycache-prefix copy is pinned by a reversal assertion I broke on purpose to confirm it has teeth, and the boundary line is pinned by three independent assertions I removed two different ways to confirm the same. The three git holes reproduce exactly as claimed and a fourth, PYTHONPATH, which round 4 declared unclosable, is closed too and I proved it with a real shadowed module rather than a missing directory. THE ONE THING THE ROUND GENUINELY GAVE UP IS GLOBAL GIT CONFIG, and it costs a workaround for a bug this item did not write, over a surface this repository does not have, in a direction that fails closed and loudly, with a local-config remedy surviving. That is a note. It deserves one header sentence naming HOME beside BASH_ENV and PATH, and it does not deserve a round. TWO SENTENCES IN THE RECORD STILL OVERSTATE, both of the exact class this item has now been corrected for five times: the environment at the boundary holds TWO variables rather than one, because CPython manufactures a constant LC_CTYPE that I proved is not attacker-controlled; and a counterfactual names four git variables as `open' that measurement shows were never false-pass routes at all. Both are resolved by deleting a clause, which is this repository's own stated remedy for an overstated sentence, and neither touches the fix, because the fix closes the CLASS regardless of which of its members happened to be exploitable. The floor is clean on every item I was asked to check and on several I added. GATE GREEN, 3201 / 0, on my own clock.
